_doc: Per-slug US label choices for tools/drugdb/fetch_fda_labels.py, kept so the weekly run does not drift back.
primary: criteria tried in order; the first one any candidate meets wins, and the normal ranking breaks ties.
alternates: secondary labels stored under alternate_labels[] in data/drugs/labels/<slug>.json (role, title, criteria).
Criterion keys (all given keys must hold): set_id, application_number (exact, or a bare prefix such as ANDA),
route (any of), form (any of), not_form (none of), brand_regex, manufacturer_regex.

text_regex is matched against the label's dosage-forms text (section 3, else description); use it to require the PH strengths. Every criterion also requires dosage_and_administration text unless require_sections is [].
require_sections [dosage_and_administration, dosage_forms_and_strengths] selects current-format (PLR) labels, which have a section 3.
Form classes: oral_ir, oral_er, oral_liquid, inj_powder, inj_solution, inj_premix (see label_forms()).
Put a set_id first once a run has confirmed the right label; keep the descriptive criteria after it as fallbacks.
none: true = never attach a US label to this slug (every US candidate is a different medicine); an existing labels/<slug>.json is removed on the next run.

iron.reason: The PH products under the bare 'iron' slug are oral iron supplements (ferrous salts registered as plain 'Iron'). The only US label openFDA matches is a homeopathic preparation (Ferrum Metallicum 6X), which is not this medicine.

hyoscine.reason: The only PH product under this slug is hyoscine butylbromide (registered as Hyoscine (as butylbromide); aliased to hyoscine-n-butylbromide). US labels for 'hyoscine' are scopolamine (hydrobromide / Transderm Scop), a different medicine. Hyoscine butylbromide has no US label.

metformin.reason: PH market is mostly immediate-release film-coated tablets (500 mg, 850 mg, 1 g); the ranking had picked Glumetza (extended-release, NDA021748).

tramadol.reason: PH oral products are immediate-release 50 mg capsules/tablets; the ranking had picked an extended-release capsule label (NDA022370).

meropenem.reason: PH products are powder for injection in vials; the ranking had picked the B. Braun DUPLEX premixed container (NDA202106). Prefer a vial label listing the PH strengths (500 mg and 1 g); the first run without that picked a 2 g-only 505(b)(2) vial (NDA215212).

vancomycin.reason: PH products are 500 mg and 1 g powder for injection in vials. The ranking had picked the Baxter GALAXY frozen premixed bag (NDA050671). The reference Vancocin vial is no longer marketed: prefer a current-format (PLR) ANDA single-dose vial label listing 500 mg and 1 g, not a pharmacy bulk package (Hospira ANDA063076 is old-format bulk) and not 505(b)(2) vials with product-specific text (Mylan NDA209481: odd strengths; Avenacy NDA210274: polysorbate 80 contraindication). No PLR ANDA single-dose vial listing both 500 mg and 1 g was found (Nov 16 2026 run), so the Avenacy vial (NDA210274) is pinned; its polysorbate 80 contraindication is product-specific.

acyclovir.reason: PH registers 200/400/800 mg tablets and 250 mg powder for IV infusion; the ranking had picked an oral suspension (ANDA217393). Oral solid label is primary; the IV label is kept as an alternate.

aciclovir.reason: Same product as acyclovir (PH INN spelling 'aciclovir' registers as a separate generic): oral IR primary, IV alternate.

ibuprofen.reason: The ranked pick (IBU tablets, ANDA075682) carries no Warnings or Precautions text in openFDA, so the NSAID kidney warnings (renal effects, hyperkalemia, advanced renal disease) were missing. PH registers 200 mg and 400 mg tablets and softgels plus 100 mg/5 mL and 200 mg/5 mL suspensions. Prefer an oral solid label that has warnings text: current-format (PLR) first, else old-format with Warnings and Precautions. The first run kept IBU because it carries a short warnings_and_cautions field; the old-format criterion (separate Warnings and Precautions) now comes first. IBU also carries a separate short warnings_and_cautions field, which the fetcher prefers over Warnings/Precautions, so its kidney warnings were still not extracted; Amneal ibuprofen tablets (ANDA078558) are tried first.

diclofenac.reason: PH market is mainly diclofenac 50 mg enteric-coated (delayed-release) tablets, plus 25 mg/mL injection, 100 mg sustained-release tablets, gel and suppositories. The ranking had picked Zipsor (diclofenac potassium 25 mg liquid-filled capsules, NDA022202), a strength and form not registered in PH. Prefer a delayed-release tablet label listing 50 mg.

zoledronic-acid.reason: 62 of 72 PH products are zoledronic acid 4 mg (powder or 4 mg/5 mL concentrate) for oncology (hypercalcemia of malignancy, myeloma, bone metastases); the ranking had picked Reclast 5 mg/100 mL (NDA021817, osteoporosis), whose kidney rules differ (contraindicated at CrCl <35 instead of the oncology CrCl dose table). Zometa-type 4 mg label is primary; Reclast is kept as an alternate for the 5 mg/100 mL products. PH 4 mg products are 4 mg/5 mL concentrate or 4 mg powder; a 4 mg/5 mL concentrate label is preferred over the 4 mg/100 mL ready-to-use bag.

alternates.title: US label: 5 mg/100 mL (osteoporosis, Paget's disease)

cefazolin.reason: PH cefazolin products are treatment vials (47 of 48). The ranking had picked WG Critical Care 2 g/3 g vials (NDA211413), a perioperative-prophylaxis label whose 8.6 says kidney dosing has not been established. Primary is the B. Braun DUPLEX treatment label (NDA050779), which carries the adult (Table 5) and pediatric (Table 6) kidney tables used on the page; the WG label is kept as an alternate for the 3 g (>=120 kg) prophylaxis dose. Pharmacology review batch 6, B6-01 (approved by Dr. Rivero, Nov 17 2026).

alternates.title: US label: 2 g and 3 g vials (perioperative prophylaxis)

cefuroxime.reason: PH registers oral cefuroxime axetil (403) and cefuroxime sodium injection (387). Oral tablet label (ANDA065308) is primary; the B. Braun DUPLEX IV label (NDA050780) is kept as an alternate because the IV kidney table (Table 2), IV hemodialysis rule and IV pediatric doses on the page come from it. Pharmacology review batch 6, B6-02 (approved by Dr. Rivero, Nov 17 2026).
